frames.text: rollers. Separate the nuts of the spring steel split spring on the roller

frames.name: p144-text-0167
frames.text: pin outside the roller until it is expanded to pass over the shoulder in

frames.name: p144-text-0168
frames.text: the road track roller pin. The road track roller and roller spring

frames.name: p144-text-0169
frames.text: plate can then be removed and the spring taken off.

frames.name: p144-text-0171
frames.text: After removing the track and drive wheel, unbolt the chain casing

frames.name: p144-text-0172
frames.text: and disconnect and remove the drive chain. Unscrew the nuts holding

frames.name: p145-text-0211
frames.text: Insert screws in the tap holes in the shaft bearing (outer end) and

frames.name: p145-text-0212
frames.text: screw them in, forcing the shaft bearing out. After the shaft bearing

frames.name: p145-text-0213
frames.text: has been removed the shaft can be drawn out and the roller pinion re-

frames.name: p145-text-0214
frames.text: moved and the floating bushings taken out.

frames.name: p145-text-0247
frames.text: Tap plug in roller pin for oil.

frames.name: p146-text-0251
frames.text: The entire control is operated from the driver’s seat, located at

frames.name: p146-text-0252
frames.text: the forward end of the hull proper. The driver’s seat and the for-

frames.name: p146-text-0253
frames.text: ward control unit, including the necessary levers, shafts, and linkage,

frames.name: p146-text-0254
frames.text: are made up as a single assembly. The driver has a pedal and four

frames.name: p146-text-0255
frames.text: levers to operate, exclusive of the spark and throttle levers. The

frames.name: p146-text-0256
frames.text: pedal is the brake. The inner left lever is a speed control for the

frames.name: p146-text-0257
frames.text: left track and the inner right lever is the speed control for the right

frames.name: p146-text-0258
frames.text: track. The outer left lever is the clutch and the outer right lever

frames.name: p146-text-0260
frames.text: The change-speed levers are similar for the left and right tracks.

frames.name: p146-text-0261
frames.text: The lever engages in two quadrant jaws, the outside taking care of

frames.name: p146-text-0262
frames.text: high speed and the inside taking care of low speed. When the lever

frames.name: p146-text-0263
frames.text: is engaged with the high or low speed jaw of the quadrant and pulled

frames.name: p146-text-0264
frames.text: back, the speed is engaged. Directions for starting and stopping are

frames.name: p146-text-0265
frames.text: given on page 14, together with driving instructions. A description

frames.name: p146-text-0266
frames.text: of the method of operation of the control system is taken up in this

frames.name: p146-text-0269
frames.text: High or low speed controls and reverse are accomplished by mov-

frames.name: p146-text-0270
frames.text: ing the speed control and reverse levers to the proper position, which

frames.name: p146-text-0271
frames.text: in turn moves a series of links which apply the high-speed or low-

frames.name: p146-text-0272
frames.text: speed brakes in the epicyclic gear, or, in the case of the reverse,

frames.name: p146-text-0273
frames.text: mesh the driving clutch on the epicyclic shaft so that the proper

frames.name: p147-text-0319
frames.text: LAYOUT OF THE CONTROL SYSTEM SHOWING LINKAGE AND LEVERS

frames.name: p148-text-0321
frames.text: The clutch lever operates the compound clutch by means of linkage

frames.name: p148-text-0322
frames.text: which extends to the throw-out-collar, and so connects that the clutch

frames.name: p148-text-0323
frames.text: is out when the lever is pulled back. As the lever is pulled back it

frames.name: p148-text-0324
frames.text: applies the brake on the cardan shaft of the clutch, as well as dis-

frames.name: p148-text-0326
frames.text: The brake pedal is interconnected by means of a swing link with

frames.name: p148-text-0327
frames.text: the shifter levers so that the brake only applies to the track which

frames.name: p148-text-0328
frames.text: is in neutral. This is accomplished by arranging the links so that

frames.name: p148-text-0329
frames.text: they are end to end when the shifter lever is in neutral position, and

frames.name: p148-text-0330
frames.text: at an angle when in high or low speed. Thus when the brake pedal

frames.name: p148-text-0331
frames.text: is applied, the links which are in a straight line or end to end transmit

frames.name: p148-text-0332
frames.text: the motion to the brake, whereas in the high or low position of the

frames.name: p148-text-0333
frames.text: shifter lever the motion of the brake pedal simply takes up the

frames.name: p148-text-0334
frames.text: linkage which is at the angle and does not communicate any motion

frames.name: p148-text-0337
frames.text: This interconnection of the linkages is made use of to accomplish

frames.name: p148-text-0338
frames.text: steering. If one track is put in neutral and the other in a forward

frames.name: p148-text-0339
frames.text: position, either high or low, and the brake is applied, the track which

frames.name: p148-text-0340
frames.text: is in neutral will be stopped, allowing the machine to be slid around

frames.name: p148-text-0341
frames.text: in the direction of the stationary track. In making turns which are

frames.name: p148-text-0342
frames.text: not as sharp it is only necessary to put one track in neutral, leaving

frames.name: p148-text-0343
frames.text: the other engaged, which will cause the machine to swing around.

frames.name: p148-text-0344
frames.text: Another method of turning in a long arc would be to have one track

frames.name: p148-text-0345
frames.text: engaged in high and the other in low, which would make one track

frames.name: p148-text-0346
frames.text: move faster than the other and consequently causing the machine to

frames.name: p148-text-0347
frames.text: turn. In other words, any difference in speed between the two tracks

frames.name: p148-text-0348
frames.text: causes the machine to swing around, and thus it is steered.

frames.name: p148-text-0350
frames.text: Mounted near the driver’s seat on the inside of the hull are the

frames.name: p148-text-0351
frames.text: spark and throttle levers as shown on page 16. These levers are

frames.name: p148-text-0352
frames.text: exactly similar, the throttle being to the right and the spark to the left.

frames.name: p148-text-0354
frames.text: The layout of the control linkage is shown on page 147. The con-

frames.name: p148-text-0355
frames.text: trol levers for operating the speeds are 37 inches in length, and are

frames.name: p148-text-0356
frames.text: of carbon steel, engaging with the carbon steel selector levers. These

frames.name: p148-text-0357
frames.text: are so shaped that they form a gate for the lever, allowing it to move

frames.name: p148-text-0358
frames.text: either the low-speed selector or the high-speed selector. As the high-

frames.name: p148-text-0359
frames.text: speed lever is pulled back it moves about a fulcrum shaft, which is

frames.name: p148-text-0360
frames.text: of carbon steel, 24¾ inches long and 1.497 inches in diameter. The

frames.name: p148-text-0361
frames.text: linkage leads back from this fulcrum shaft to a shaft in the center of

frames.name: p148-text-0362
frames.text: the machine, which serves to break the length of the link rods. By

frames.name: p149-text-0364
frames.text: means of clevis connections and toggle joints the control is passed

frames.name: p149-text-0365
frames.text: along backward to the high and low speed brake toggles, which operate

frames.name: p149-text-0366
frames.text: the control brakes on the high and low speed drums of the epicyclic

frames.name: p149-text-0369
frames.text: The track brakes are on each side of the epicyclic, just inside the

frames.name: p149-text-0370
frames.text: chain sprocket, on the epicyclic shaft. As briefly explained, the link-

frames.name: p149-text-0371
frames.text: age of the brake is so arranged that only the brake on the side in

frames.name: p149-text-0372
frames.text: neutral is applied. The linkage is so interconnected that when the

frames.name: p149-text-0373
frames.text: shifter lever is moved to neutral, the brake bands just clear the drum.

frames.name: p149-text-0374
frames.text: Application of pressure on the pedal, therefore, results in immediate

frames.name: p149-text-0375
frames.text: pressure on the drum. The brake pedal is a malleable-iron casting

frames.name: p149-text-0376
frames.text: 35¼ inches long over all, the pedal being 8 inches long by 5 inches

frames.name: p149-text-0377
frames.text: wide, I-section. The connections of this pedal, which is a bell crank,

frames.name: p149-text-0378
frames.text: connected with a series of toggles and links, are clearly illustrated on

frames.name: p149-text-0379
frames.text: page 147. The brake rods are held back in three sections as in the

frames.name: p149-text-0380
frames.text: case of the other control rods, so as to break their length, and at the

frames.name: p149-text-0381
frames.text: same time secure the necessary reduction.

frames.name: p149-text-0383
frames.text: The clutch lever is a carbon steel lever in the form of a bell crank.

frames.name: p149-text-0384
frames.text: The hand end is 28½ inches long from the center of the fulcrum to

frames.name: p149-text-0385
frames.text: the end. The bell-crank end is 5 inches long. This connects with

frames.name: p149-text-0386
frames.text: the toggle joint, mounted on the shaft, directly behind the lever

frames.name: p150-text-0390
frames.text: fulcrum shaft, and the rods extent backward to the main clutch

frames.name: p150-text-0391
frames.text: operating the clutch throw-out lever, which removes the cone from

frames.name: p150-text-0392
frames.text: engagement with the flywheel and also the driving box on the clutch

frames.name: p150-text-0395
frames.text: The reverse lever is a carbon steel piece of bell-crank form, being

frames.name: p150-text-0396
frames.text: 27.968 inches long on the hand side of the fulcrum and 6 inches on

frames.name: p150-text-0397
frames.text: the bell crank. It engages with the reverse rod, which is 52 inches

frames.name: p150-text-0398
frames.text: long, and made of extra strong ¾-inch wrought-iron pipe. Similar

frames.name: p150-text-0399
frames.text: to the other control rods, this is in three sections, front, center, and

frames.name: p150-text-0400
frames.text: rear, carrying the motion of the reverse lever back to the rear control

frames.text: or clevices of the control rods. The adjustment can most easily be

frames.text: lock nut and turning the fork end to the desired location.

frames.text: brake band (short end), passing up from the under side of brake.

frames.text: One end of the brake lever is connected with the rear control rod;

frames.text: high-speed brake suspension spring between the brake lever and the

frames.text: The first adjustments are made by screwing up on the fork ends or

frames.text: clevices of the control rods, the fork ends between the front and center

frames.name: p154-text-0458
frames.text: control rods, underneath the center ammunition storage being where

frames.text: the adjustment can most easily be made, by slacking the lock nut and

frames.text: The final adjustment is made on the low-speed brake band by means

frames.text: and is fastened by a pin to the low-gear brake-band ear (upper), the

frames.text: After removing the epicyclic gear from machine, disconnect the

frames.text: high-speed brake and remove in the following order:

frames.text: Remove cotter pins from the free end pins and drive out the pins

frames.text: Remove the bottom band stop by unscrewing the top bolt holding

frames.text: Unscrew the tap bolts holding the top band stop to the epicyclic

frames.text: frame. The top band stop and backband stop can then be removed.

frames.text: Remove cotter pin and drive out anchor pin. Unscrew tap bolts

frames.text: Rotate strap around clockwise to remove the six ⅜-inch set

frames.text: screws, uncoupling the long and short end brake bands which would

frames.text: Shear the rivet heads and remove the old lining.

frames.name: p154-text-0484

frames.name: p154-text-0485
frames.text: and drive out the brake pins from the upper and lower free ends of

frames.text: Remove the brake stop by unscrewing the nut of the bolt fastening

frames.text: The reduction of the brake linkage for the epicyclic gear and for the

frames.name: p159-text-0665
frames.text: CONTROL ROD ENDS WITH EPICYCLIC TRANSMISSION REMOVED FROM HULL

frames.name: p160-text-0669
frames.text: The Mark VIII machine is equipped with Bijur starting and light-

frames.name: p160-text-0670
frames.text: ing apparatus designed for operation with a 6-volt battery and con-

frames.name: p160-text-0672
frames.text: One (1) type L–61 M–1108 anticlock rotation lighting genera-

frames.name: p160-text-0674
frames.text: One (1) type AD–200 M–923 anticlock rotation starting

frames.name: p160-text-0676
frames.text: One (1) type TI–61 M–865 motor starting switch.

frames.name: p160-text-0677
frames.text: The generator is in operation at all times the engine is in operation.

frames.name: p160-text-0678
frames.text: The starting motor is in operation only during the period of start-

frames.name: p160-text-0681
frames.text: Page 161 shows the wiring layout on the machine and covers the

frames.name: p160-text-0682
frames.text: ignition generator (Delco make) as well as the wiring for the Bijur

frames.name: p160-text-0684
frames.text: The Bijur generator is grounded internally and only one cable

frames.name: p160-text-0685
frames.text: leads from same, the frame of the machine acting as a common

frames.name: p160-text-0686
frames.text: return conductor. The generator is connected direct to the battery,

frames.name: p160-text-0687
frames.text: as no fuse is required in the generator battery circuit.

frames.name: p160-text-0688
frames.text: The circuit between the storage battery, starting switch, and the

frames.name: p160-text-0689
frames.text: starting motor is made up with heavy cable, and this circuit does

frames.name: p160-text-0690
frames.text: not make use of the machine frame as a return circuit.

frames.name: p160-text-0692
frames.text: The starting motor using a 6-volt 140-ampere hour battery is not

frames.name: p160-text-0693
frames.text: intended to crank the gas motor when cold without manual help at

frames.name: p161-text-0003
frames.text: First, see that all necessary adjustments for the gas motor have

frames.name: p161-text-0004
frames.text: been made; insert the hand crank and exert upward; pull on crank.

frames.name: p161-text-0005
frames.text: When ready to start, signal operator at the starting switch to depress

frames.name: p161-text-0006
frames.text: starting-switch button, at the same time giving the motor all possible

frames.name: p161-text-0008
frames.text: The starting switch should be depressed downward as far as it will

frames.name: p161-text-0009
frames.text: go and held firmly in place until the gas engine begins firing. The

frames.name: p161-text-0010
frames.text: instant the gas engine begins firing, release the starting-switch but-

frames.name: p161-text-0011
frames.text: ton. Should the gas motor fail to start promptly after cranking it

frames.name: p161-text-0012
frames.text: with the starting motor, do not continue to crank it, but first see

frames.name: p161-text-0013
frames.text: that proper adjustments for starting have been made, that there is

frames.name: p161-text-0014
frames.text: gasoline in the carburetor, and that the ignition is in working order.

frames.name: p161-text-0015
frames.text: Continued cranking of the gas engine with the electric starter will

frames.name: p161-text-0016
frames.text: not damage the electrical equipment but constitutes a useless drain

frames.name: p161-text-0017
frames.text: on the battery and should be avoided.

frames.name: p161-text-0019
frames.text: WIRING OF LIGHTING, STARTING, AND IGNITION

frames.name: p162-text-0024
frames.text: The starting motor is a series wound, four-pole machine designed

frames.name: p162-text-0025
frames.text: for operation on a 6-volt battery, and is equipped with a Bijur

frames.name: p162-text-0026
frames.text: automatic pinion-shifting device mounted on its armature shaft for

frames.name: p162-text-0027
frames.text: transmitting power from the starting motor to the flywheel.

frames.name: p162-text-0028
frames.text: No intermediate linkage or preliminary contact resistance switch

frames.name: p162-text-0029
frames.text: is required to bring the pinion of the starter motor into mesh

frames.name: p162-text-0030
frames.text: with the flywheel teeth to crank the gas motor. A double-contact

frames.name: p162-text-0031
frames.text: single-pole switch connects the starting motor directly across the

frames.name: p162-text-0032
frames.text: battery and the instant that the switch is closed cranking is auto-

frames.name: p162-text-0034
frames.text: When the starting-switch pedal is depressed the starting motor

frames.name: p162-text-0035
frames.text: to battery circuit is closed and the machine begins to operate under

frames.name: p162-text-0036
frames.text: full power, the pinion shifting device mounted on the threaded end

frames.name: p162-text-0037
frames.text: of the armature shaft automatically meshing with and transmitting

frames.name: p162-text-0038
frames.text: power to the flywheel teeth, thus cranking the gas motor.

frames.name: p162-text-0039
frames.text: The instant that gas motor begins firing, the overriding speed at

frames.name: p162-text-0040
frames.text: which the starter pinion is driven by the flywheel with respect to the

frames.name: p162-text-0041
frames.text: armature shaft causes the device automatically to travel along the

frames.name: p162-text-0042
frames.text: threaded shaft and disengage the flywheel teeth.

frames.name: p163-text-0089
frames.text: The pinion-shifting device is positive in every respect and will

frames.name: p163-text-0090
frames.text: crank the gas motor every time the starting switch is closed. It is

frames.name: p163-text-0091
frames.text: impossible under normal operating conditions for the starting pinion

frames.name: p163-text-0092
frames.text: to “butt” or “jam” against the teeth of the flywheel, as the pinion

frames.name: p163-text-0093
frames.text: will always go into mesh with the flywheel teeth for reasons which

frames.name: p163-text-0095
frames.text: The operation and construction of the automatic gear-shifting

frames.name: p163-text-0096
frames.text: device used in connection with the starting motor may be best under-

frames.name: p163-text-0097
frames.text: stood by reference to B/P 138 and the description that is to follow:

frames.name: p163-text-0098
frames.text: Referring to page 162, the pinion mentioned above shown by Figure

frames.name: p163-text-0099
frames.text: No. 4 is driven by notches in the barrel (6) registering with the

frames.name: p163-text-0100
frames.text: pinion teeth. This barrel has 6 slots cut about ¾ inch deep in its

frames.name: p163-text-0101
frames.text: other end, in which the notched clutch plate (12) registers. The

frames.name: p163-text-0102
frames.text: cork clutch (13) is held in place against (12) by means of the notched

frames.name: p163-text-0103
frames.text: retainer (27) and its right-hand face can slip slightly against the

frames.name: p163-text-0104
frames.text: smooth ground face of the flanged nut (14) whenever the torque

frames.name: p163-text-0105
frames.text: exceeds the frictional hold between the cork and steel faces, this

frames.name: p163-text-0106
frames.text: holding force being set up by the initially compressed spring (11).

frames.name: p163-text-0107
frames.text: Power is thus transmitted in the working position from the shaft

frames.name: p163-text-0108
frames.text: to the flanged nut (14), thence to the clutch (13), the retainer (27),

frames.name: p163-text-0109
frames.text: clutch plate (12), barrel (6), and thus to pinion (4).

frames.name: p164-text-0113
frames.text: The cover (19), which fits into and over the notched barrel (6),

frames.name: p164-text-0114
frames.text: effects closure of the shift when locked in place by spring cover lock

frames.name: p164-text-0116
frames.text: In addition to the cork clutch there is a fixed clutch mounted on the

frames.name: p164-text-0117
frames.text: other face of the pinion flange and shown at (15). This clutch is

frames.name: p164-text-0118
frames.text: held against the flange by means of the clutch-spring washer (16),

frames.name: p164-text-0119
frames.text: sleeve (17) and wire-lock spring (18). It is called “fixed” because

frames.name: p164-text-0120
frames.text: the torque necessary to cause it to slip is constant irrespective of the

frames.name: p164-text-0122
frames.text: Normal entrance is effected by depressing the starting-switch

frames.name: p164-text-0123
frames.text: pedal, causing the shaft to rotate within the flanged nut (14), the

frames.name: p164-text-0124
frames.text: inertia of which causes a difference in speed between the shaft and the

frames.name: p164-text-0125
frames.text: nut with the result that the nut travels along the threaded shaft (28)

frames.name: p164-text-0126
frames.text: and urges the entire assembly of barrel and pinion through the

frames.name: p164-text-0127
frames.text: spring (11) into mesh. The spring (11) rests at its left-hand end

frames.name: p164-text-0128
frames.text: against a flanged plate (5) riveted to the pinion. When the nut gets

frames.name: p164-text-0129
frames.text: to the end of its stroke it first compresses a pair of dished washers

frames.name: p164-text-0130
frames.text: (shown at 8) through a pair of thrust-bearing washers (9) and (26).

frames.name: p164-text-0131
frames.text: It is the combined object of the dished washers, as well as the clutch,

frames.name: p164-text-0132
frames.text: to take up the shock of starting. The helical spring (11) plays little,

frames.name: p164-text-0133
frames.text: if any, role in this. Of course, when the clutch face rises enormously,

frames.name: p164-text-0134
frames.text: that is, to say, the clutch becomes self-tightening to meet the load

frames.name: p164-text-0136
frames.text: Coming out of mesh is caused by the overriding speed of the

frames.name: p164-text-0137
frames.text: pinion barrel and flanged nut assembly with respect to the revolving

frames.name: p164-text-0138
frames.text: armature shaft. The outcoming blow is cushioned by the spring (21)

frames.name: p164-text-0140
frames.text: The purpose of the clutch plate (15) is to get sufficient initial

frames.name: p164-text-0141
frames.text: clutch tension added to the clutch (13) to avoid slippage when a

frames.name: p164-text-0143
frames.text: Whenever a pinion tooth “butts,” that is, strikes the corresponding

frames.name: p164-text-0144
frames.text: end of a flywheel tooth, this interference is almost constantly over-

frames.name: p164-text-0145
frames.text: come by the following action which takes place: The pinion is now

frames.name: p164-text-0146
frames.text: kept from entering the flywheel teeth and the traveling nut compresses

frames.name: p164-text-0147
frames.text: the spring (11), urging the notched barrel (6) forward along the teeth

frames.name: p164-text-0148
frames.text: of the pinion. Finally, the clutch plate (12) strikes the washer (26)

frames.name: p164-text-0149
frames.text: locking up, or rather tightening, the clutch (13), and in turn causes

frames.name: p164-text-0150
frames.text: the nut (14) to turn with the shaft. The barrel (6) is therefore

frames.name: p164-text-0151
frames.text: turned by the notched plate (12) and in turn transmits its rotative

frames.name: p164-text-0152
frames.text: effort to the pinion (4), releasing the “butting” pinion tooth from its

frames.name: p164-text-0153
frames.text: interference. The instant this happens the spring (11) having been

frames.name: p164-text-0154
frames.text: greatly compressed by the previous action, snaps the offending tooth

frames.name: p164-text-0155
frames.text: into mesh with the flywheel and normal cranking takes place.

frames.name: p164-text-0156
frames.text: The function of the weak springs (3) is to prevent “ticking in” of

frames.name: p164-text-0157
frames.text: the barrel and pinion, especially when the tank is running down hill.

frames.name: p165-text-0160
frames.text: The shift should always be checked for the gap between the edge

frames.name: p165-text-0161
frames.text: of the flywheel and the pinion teeth. This distance must always

frames.name: p165-text-0162
frames.text: be ⅜ inch. In testing the shift, run the barrel along the threads by

frames.name: p165-text-0163
frames.text: hand and note whether there is the proper freedom of action, that is,

frames.name: p165-text-0164
frames.text: whether the shaft is free from burrs or rust. Care should be taken

frames.name: p165-text-0165
frames.text: that there is sufficient lubricant, oil, or graphite on the threads of the

frames.name: p165-text-0166
frames.text: armature shaft (28) and between washers (9) and (26), washers (23)

frames.name: p165-text-0168
frames.text: In order to test the shift for initial torque of its clutches, a brake

frames.name: p165-text-0169
frames.text: should be made to fit over the pinion (4) having a lever arm 1 foot

frames.name: p165-text-0170
frames.text: in length. The armature shaft can then be held from turning by

frames.name: p165-text-0171
frames.text: means of an open wrench on the commutator end hexagon shaft nut

frames.name: p165-text-0172
frames.text: and force applied by hand to the end of the brake arm through a

frames.name: p165-text-0173
frames.text: spring scale with the barrel in the “out” position. The number of

frames.name: p165-text-0174
frames.text: foot-pounds necessary to slip the barrel in this “out” position should

frames.name: p165-text-0175
frames.text: always be greater than 4½ to 5 pounds on the scale and may, how-

frames.name: p165-text-0176
frames.text: ever, be as much as to 12 or 15 pounds without affecting the correct

frames.name: p165-text-0177
frames.text: functioning of the shift. If it is less than 4½ pounds a dangerous

frames.name: p165-text-0178
frames.text: condition arises in case there is too tight meshing of the pinion in the

frames.name: p165-text-0179
frames.text: flywheel. Such cases frequently require 8 to 10 pounds initial

frames.name: p165-text-0180
frames.text: clutch torque to cause the pinion to enter and a 4½-pound clutch

frames.name: p165-text-0183
frames.text: (1) Slipping clutches.—There are two forms of clutch slip. The

frames.name: p165-text-0184
frames.text: first is initial clutch slip, which has just been described, and the

frames.name: p165-text-0185
frames.text: second is clutch slip, which takes place in the “in” position.

frames.name: p165-text-0186
frames.text: In the first case three-quarters of the initial clutch value lies in the

frames.name: p165-text-0187
frames.text: outside or fixed clutch applied through the dished spring washer (16).

frames.name: p165-text-0188
frames.text: It is usual to look here or in the length of the sleeve (17) for the cause

frames.name: p165-text-0189
frames.text: of intial clutch torque weakness. In the case of clutch slipping when

frames.name: p165-text-0190
frames.text: in cranking or “in” position this can be attributed either to a great

frames.name: p165-text-0191
frames.text: excess of oil or lubricant on the cork face of the clutch or to a mutilated

frames.name: p165-text-0192
frames.text: cork surface. In case the projections on back of retainer (27) shear

frames.name: p165-text-0193
frames.text: in clutch plate (12), slippage is likely to occur, and can be remedied

frames.name: p165-text-0194
frames.text: only by supplying a new retainer.

frames.name: p165-text-0195
frames.text: (2) Sticking.—This can happen either in the “in” or “out”

frames.name: p165-text-0196
frames.text: position. In the “out” position it is usually caused by too tight a

frames.name: p165-text-0197
frames.text: fit of the flanged nut on the armature-shaft threads, and can be

frames.name: p165-text-0198
frames.text: determined as aforesaid by revolving the barrel on the threads, to

frames.name: p165-text-0199
frames.text: feel if the mechanism is free, or it may be due to dirt on the face of

frames.name: p165-text-0200
frames.text: the thrust washer (23) which the flanged nut strikes in this position.

frames.name: p165-text-0201
frames.text: The remedy is this: Remove the nut (25) and thoroughly clean

frames.name: p165-text-0202
frames.text: parts (23) and (24) as well as the back of the flanged nut. Be sure

frames.name: p166-text-0204
frames.text: to place graphite between washers (23) and (24) when reassembling.

frames.name: p166-text-0205
frames.text: If the flanged nut is not perfectly free on the threaded shaft, dis-

frames.name: p166-text-0206
frames.text: assemble the entire shift, beginning with spring lock (20), and “lap

frames.name: p166-text-0207
frames.text: in” the nut on the threads, using a mixture of kerosene and emery

frames.name: p166-text-0208
frames.text: dust. Be sure to clean the shaft and nut carefully with gasoline

frames.name: p166-text-0209
frames.text: before reassembling. Washers (9) and (26) leave the factory with

frames.name: p166-text-0210
frames.text: graphite between their faces and it is always well to make sure that

frames.name: p166-text-0211
frames.text: some is put between them before reassembling, especially after clean-

frames.name: p166-text-0212
frames.text: ing the shaft with gasoline. When disassembling it is not necessary

frames.name: p166-text-0213
frames.text: to disturb the various parts mounted on the flanged nut.

frames.name: p166-text-0214
frames.text: Stick in the “out” position can also be caused by the back nut (25)

frames.name: p166-text-0215
frames.text: becoming loose. This makes the “out” stop take place between the

frames.name: p166-text-0216
frames.text: back end of pinion (4) and shaft nut (7) instead of between the faces of

frames.name: p166-text-0217
frames.text: (24) and (25). Sticking here occurs because the parts (4) and (7) are

frames.name: p166-text-0218
frames.text: relatively soft, and any hammering or rubbing of the pinion (4) against

frames.name: p166-text-0219
frames.text: the face of shaft collar (25) will roughen the butting faces, causing

frames.name: p166-text-0220
frames.text: sticking. There is a gap between (4) and (7) in normal working of

frames.name: p166-text-0222
frames.text: Sticking in the “in” position may be due to dirt or grit getting

frames.name: p166-text-0223
frames.text: between the washers (9) and (26) on inside of the barrel, spring lock

frames.name: p166-text-0224
frames.text: (10) becoming dislocated, or clutch plate (12) cutting into washer (26).

frames.name: p166-text-0225
frames.text: Be sure that the striking face of clutch plate (12) is polished clean and

frames.name: p166-text-0226
frames.text: that plenty of graphite and lubricant are between washers (9) and

frames.name: p166-text-0227
frames.text: (26). In case the striking face of (12) and the inside washer (26) are

frames.name: p166-text-0228
frames.text: cutting each other, it is best to communicate with the factory and

frames.name: p166-text-0230
frames.text: (3) Shock.—This may be due to the flattening of washers (8), or,

frames.name: p166-text-0231
frames.text: where too tight, gripping action of clutch (13) occurs. In the case

frames.name: p166-text-0232
frames.text: of washer flattening, do not attempt to repair these, but replace with

frames.name: p166-text-0233
frames.text: new ones. A very little graphite or oil applied to the cork clutch

frames.name: p166-text-0234
frames.text: surface will usually remedy a tight clutch and reduce shock.

frames.name: p166-text-0235
frames.text: (4) Precautions.—In making repairs to shift do not replace any

frames.name: p166-text-0236
frames.text: defective or worn parts other than those supplied directly from the

frames.name: p166-text-0237
frames.text: Bijur factory. All the parts making up complete assembly are either

frames.name: p166-text-0238
frames.text: made of special material or are given a special heat treatment, and

frames.name: p166-text-0239
frames.text: the substitution of inferior or improperly treated materials will not

frames.name: p166-text-0240
frames.text: allow the satisfactory operation of the shift.

frames.name: p166-text-0243
frames.text: This is a self-contained unit with no regulator or automatic cut-out

frames.name: p166-text-0244
frames.text: requiring separate mounting and adjusting. The automatic switch

frames.name: p166-text-0245
frames.text: for opening and closing the circuit between the storage battery and

frames.name: p166-text-0246
frames.text: the generator is mounted inside of the generator. The regulation of

frames.name: p166-text-0247
frames.text: the so-called constant current generator is inherent and no separate

frames.name: p167-text-0250
frames.text: The amount of current generated is, to a large extent, independent

frames.name: p167-text-0251
frames.text: of the state of charge of the storage battery or the amount of lamp

frames.name: p167-text-0252
frames.text: load connected, but depends primarily upon the speed at which

frames.name: p167-text-0253
frames.text: machine is driven and the position of the regulating brush with respect

frames.name: p167-text-0255
frames.text: Beginning at zero speed, the voltage is of course zero, and with

frames.name: p167-text-0256
frames.text: increasing speed the voltage increases until the armature develops

frames.name: p167-text-0257
frames.text: 6.5 volts, at which value the shunt coil of the cut-out is sufficiently

frames.name: p167-text-0258
frames.text: energized to cause the cut-out switch to close.

frames.name: p167-text-0259
frames.text: After the cut-out is closed the generator begins to deliver current to

frames.name: p167-text-0260
frames.text: the battery or to both the battery and the light, if lights are in use.

frames.name: p167-text-0261
frames.text: The point at which the cut-out closes (6.5 volts) corresponds to

frames.name: p167-text-0262
frames.text: approximately 500 to 600 generator r. p. m. With increasing speed

frames.name: p167-text-0263
frames.text: the current increases to a maximum value, at speeds of about 1,400 to

frames.name: p167-text-0264
frames.text: 1,600 r. p. m.; at higher speeds the current decreases slightly.

frames.name: p167-text-0265
frames.text: The constant current generator has a single shunt winding dis-

frames.name: p167-text-0266
frames.text: tributed over four poles and the regulation is effected by having this

frames.name: p167-text-0267
frames.text: winding connected between one of the main generator brushes and an

frames.name: p167-text-0268
frames.text: auxiliary or regulating brush, and about 60° from this main brush.

frames.name: p167-text-0269
frames.text: The maximum current generated depends upon the location of the

frames.name: p167-text-0270
frames.text: third brush with respect to the main brush to which one side of the

frames.name: p167-text-0271
frames.text: shunt field is connected. Moving the third, or regulating brush, in

frames.name: p167-text-0272
frames.text: the direction of rotation of the armature increases the generator

frames.name: p167-text-0273
frames.text: output, and in direction opposite to the rotation of armature

frames.name: p167-text-0276
frames.text: Referring to page 163, showing the commutator end housing of

frames.name: p167-text-0277
frames.text: the type L–61 generator, and considered for clearness to be trans-

frames.name: p167-text-0278
frames.text: parent, the third brush and the two main brushes are indicated by

frames.name: p167-text-0279
frames.text: name, the third brush adjusting hole at B, and the main switch-

frames.name: p167-text-0280
frames.text: adjusting nut at A. Figure 165 shows all internal connections for

frames.name: p167-text-0281
frames.text: the shunt winding, brushes, and the main switch.

frames.name: p167-text-0282
frames.text: Due to the fact that the voltage regulation of all third brush

frames.name: p167-text-0283
frames.text: generators is effected by means of the reaction magnetic flux set

frames.name: p167-text-0284
frames.text: up by the current flowing through the armature, it is necessary to

frames.name: p167-text-0285
frames.text: introduce some protective device, such as a fuse in the field circuit,

frames.name: p167-text-0286
frames.text: in order to prevent too great an increase in voltage across the field

frames.name: p167-text-0287
frames.text: in case of an accidental loose or open battery connection. With

frames.name: p167-text-0288
frames.text: the battery connected to the generator and all cable connections

frames.name: p167-text-0289
frames.text: making good contact, the current flowing through the armature

frames.name: p167-text-0290
frames.text: produces the necessary reaction and effects regulation holding down

frames.name: p167-text-0291
frames.text: the voltage to a normal value.

frames.name: p167-text-0292
frames.text: When the generator is disconnected from the battery for any

frames.name: p167-text-0293
frames.text: length of time, the reaction normally set up by the armature ap-

frames.name: p168-text-0295
frames.text: proaches a zero value, thereby causing a greatly increased e. m. f.

frames.name: p168-text-0296
frames.text: to be developed by armature conductors between the main and third

frames.name: p168-text-0297
frames.text: brush across which the field windings are connected. The net result

frames.name: p168-text-0298
frames.text: under these conditions is an increased field exciting current approach-

frames.name: p168-text-0299
frames.text: ing in value the normal output rating of the machine, and conse-

frames.name: p168-text-0300
frames.text: quently a greatly increased terminal voltage developed. As the

frames.name: p168-text-0301
frames.text: value of the current required for field excitation is quite small in

frames.name: p168-text-0302
frames.text: comparison with the generator output, the field windings would not

frames.name: p168-text-0303
frames.text: stand this overvoltage in case of an open battery connection for

frames.name: p168-text-0304
frames.text: any length of time, and a fuse of 8 to 12 ampere capacity is there-

frames.name: p168-text-0305
frames.text: fore connected in the field circuit to protect the winding. This fuse

frames.name: p168-text-0306
frames.text: is held in place by two phosphor-bronze clips, the entire assembly

frames.name: p168-text-0307
frames.text: being protected by a nickel-plated cover, as shown on Diagram 164.

frames.name: p168-text-0308
frames.text: It is not feasible to supply lamps directly from a constant current

frames.name: p168-text-0309
frames.text: generator with battery disconnected unless the lamps so connected

frames.name: p168-text-0310
frames.text: consume the entire current output of the machine. If the current

frames.name: p168-text-0311
frames.text: required to supply the lamps is less than the generator output the

frames.name: p168-text-0312
frames.text: lamps will be burned out. For instance, if the generator output

frames.name: p168-text-0313
frames.text: is 15 amperes and the current consumed by the lights is 7 amperes,

frames.name: p168-text-0314
frames.text: the generator voltage will rise until the additional 8 amperes not

frames.name: p168-text-0315
frames.text: required by the lamps will be forced through the lamp circuit. This

frames.name: p168-text-0316
frames.text: will naturally overload the lamps and burn them out. No attempt

frames.name: p168-text-0317
frames.text: should, therefore, be made to operate lamps direct from a constant

frames.name: p168-text-0318
frames.text: current generator without using a storage battery in conjunction

frames.name: p168-text-0321
frames.text: Start the engine, allow it to run at a speed sufficient to obtain a

frames.name: p168-text-0322
frames.text: generator r. p. m. of 1,000 or more and with a test ammeter con-

frames.name: p168-text-0323
frames.text: nected between the cable leading to generator and the terminal of

frames.name: p168-text-0324
frames.text: generator, observe the output. This output should not be less than

frames.name: p168-text-0326
frames.text: Before making any adjustment, test the battery with a hydrometer

frames.name: p168-text-0327
frames.text: and carefully inspect the brushes to see that they are seated properly

frames.name: p168-text-0328
frames.text: on the commutator and that they are free to move up and down in

frames.name: p168-text-0329
frames.text: their respective holders. Also inspect the commutator to see that

frames.name: p168-text-0330
frames.text: it is clean and that the mica insulation between bars is properly

frames.name: p168-text-0331
frames.text: undercut, as high mica and dirt will prevent satisfactory operation

frames.name: p168-text-0333
frames.text: If the specific gravity of the battery is 1.25 or above, and the

frames.name: p168-text-0334
frames.text: generator is delivering from 12 and 14 amperes at this speed, no

frames.name: p168-text-0336
frames.text: The arrangement of the brushes and cut-out switch in the front

frames.name: p168-text-0337
frames.text: head of the generator is shown on blue print 164 and all symbols used

frames.name: p168-text-0338
frames.text: in the following instructions will be found on this blue print.

frames.name: p169-text-0340
frames.text: ADJUSTING THE GENERATOR SWITCH OR CUT-OUT

frames.name: p169-text-0341
frames.text: First, see that the main switch or cut-out connects the generator

frames.name: p169-text-0342
frames.text: to the battery at the proper voltage. The speed of generator need

frames.name: p169-text-0343
frames.text: not be considered in making this check, but with a test voltmeter

frames.name: p169-text-0344
frames.text: connected across the two main brushes of machine measure the

frames.name: p169-text-0345
frames.text: voltage at the instant the test ammeter, already connected in circuit,

frames.name: p169-text-0346
frames.text: begins to show a charge. The correct voltage at which the main

frames.name: p169-text-0347
frames.text: switch closes is 6.5 volts, and if the voltage is above or below this

frames.name: p169-text-0348
frames.text: value switch should be adjusted by inserting a small fiber handle

frames.name: p169-text-0349
frames.text: socket wrench in the adjusting hole at “A” and turning the tension-

frames.name: p169-text-0350
frames.text: spring adjusting nut until the switch closes at the correct voltage.

frames.name: p169-text-0352
frames.text: The current output of the generator when driven at speeds of

frames.name: p169-text-0353
frames.text: 1,400 to 1,600 r. p. m. should not be less than 12 or more than 15

frames.name: p169-text-0354
frames.text: amperes, and its output should be adjusted accordingly.

frames.name: p169-text-0355
frames.text: It is not necessary to remove the generator for adjusting. The

frames.name: p169-text-0356
frames.text: third or regulating brush is so arranged that by inserting a special

frames.name: p169-text-0357
frames.text: tooth-adjusting wrench (B–4 260–M) the adjusting hole at B and

frames.name: p169-text-0358
frames.text: engaging the ratchet (6) the entire regulating brush assembly can

frames.name: p169-text-0359
frames.text: be shifted in a direction required.

frames.name: p169-text-0360
frames.text: Before attempting to adjust, remove the cable from the generator

frames.name: p169-text-0361
frames.text: terminal and connect a standard test ammeter between the generator

frames.name: p169-text-0362
frames.text: and cable removed and note the value of current. If the current

frames.name: p169-text-0363
frames.text: delivered by the generator is less than 12 or more than 16 amperes,

frames.name: p169-text-0365
frames.text: Moving the regulating brush assembly in direction opposite to

frames.name: p169-text-0366
frames.text: the rotation of the generator’s armature decreases the current output

frames.name: p169-text-0367
frames.text: and in the same direction of armature rotation increases the output.

frames.name: p169-text-0368
frames.text: To get the best results, the setting should be made when the

frames.name: p169-text-0369
frames.text: generator is hot and connected to a battery having a specific gravity.

frames.name: p169-text-0371
frames.text: In order to maintain the following:

frames.name: p169-text-0375
frames.text: 4. Free movement of the brushes in their holders.

frames.name: p169-text-0376
frames.text: 5. Good contact of brushes with the commutator.

frames.name: p169-text-0378
frames.text: 1. A few drops of thin neutral oil should be put into the oilers of

frames.name: p169-text-0379
frames.text: the generator after every two weeks. This will insure proper lubri-

frames.name: p169-text-0380
frames.text: cation of the bearings and prevent freezing to the armature shaft.

frames.name: p170-text-0383
frames.text: 2. After the generator has been run for a length of time, carbon

frames.name: p170-text-0384
frames.text: dust will accumulate on the brushes and brush holders, which will

frames.name: p170-text-0385
frames.text: tend to destroy their useful functions. Wear on the brushes is

frames.name: p170-text-0386
frames.text: natural and the dust caused by same can not be avoided from col-

frames.name: p170-text-0387
frames.text: lecting on the parts inside the generator. It is possible for oil from

frames.name: p170-text-0388
frames.text: the bearings or other sources to reach the inside of the generator and

frames.name: p170-text-0389
frames.text: mix with the carbon dust, forming a gummy paste which readily

frames.name: p170-text-0390
frames.text: adheres to the brushes and holders. This paste can be removed by

frames.name: p170-text-0391
frames.text: washing the brushes in gasoline and removing from the brush holders

frames.name: p170-text-0392
frames.text: with a cloth soaked in gasoline.

frames.name: p170-text-0393
frames.text: 3. The surface of the commutator should be free from oil and dirt.

frames.name: p170-text-0394
frames.text: To clean the commutator, run the engine at a moderate speed, and

frames.name: p170-text-0395
frames.text: with No. 00 sandpaper cut into thin strips remove any dirt or soil

frames.name: p170-text-0396
frames.text: that may have collected. Do not use emery cloth or cloth. Never

frames.name: p170-text-0397
frames.text: put lubricant of any kind on the commutator. After cleaning, be

frames.name: p170-text-0398
frames.text: sure that all the sand particles from the sandpaper have been blown

frames.name: p170-text-0400
frames.text: 4. The brushes, when replaced in their holders, should be free to

frames.name: p170-text-0402
frames.text: 5. Seating of the brushes can quickly be accomplished by placing

frames.name: p170-text-0403
frames.text: a thin strip of No. 00 sandpaper under the brush with the sanded

frames.name: p170-text-0404
frames.text: side of the paper against the commutator bearing surface of the brush

frames.name: p170-text-0405
frames.text: and drawn from under brush against the rotation of the armature.

frames.name: p170-text-0406
frames.text: Pressure of the brush springs is sufficient to cause the sandpaper to

frames.name: p170-text-0407
frames.text: sear brushes and it is not necessary to apply extra pressure on the

frames.name: p170-text-0408
frames.text: tops of brushes with the fingers.

frames.name: p170-text-0409
frames.text: 6. See that the brush springs are away from the head casting or

frames.name: p170-text-0410
frames.text: screws that would cause a ground, and that they bear upon tops of

frames.name: p170-text-0411
frames.text: brushes at the center. This will insure proper pressure exerted on

frames.name: p171-text-0416
frames.text: The ammunition storage capacity of the Mark VIII machine is

frames.name: p171-text-0417
frames.text: 21,000 rounds of machine-gun ammunition and 208 rounds of 6-

frames.name: p171-text-0418
frames.text: pounder ammunition. Of the 208 rounds of 6-pounder ammunition,

frames.name: p171-text-0419
frames.text: 26 rounds are smoke shells and the balance are common shells.

frames.name: p171-text-0421
frames.text: There are five places for storing the 6-pounder ammunition, one in

frames.name: p171-text-0422
frames.text: each sponson, one on each side of the driver, and one in the center

frames.name: p171-text-0423
frames.text: of the fighting compartment. The top rows of 6-pounder shells in

frames.name: p171-text-0424
frames.text: the sponsons are smoke shells. These shells go into cylindrical cases,

frames.name: p171-text-0425
frames.text: designed to fit them, and from which they can be removed readily.

frames.name: p171-text-0426
frames.text: The capacity of each of the sponson magazines or ammunition stor-

frames.name: p171-text-0427
frames.text: age spaces are six smoke shells on each side of the sponson underneath

frames.name: p171-text-0428
frames.text: the gun and seven smoke shells at rear of sponson, giving 13 smoke

frames.name: p171-text-0429
frames.text: shells on each side, or 26 total.

frames.name: p171-text-0430
frames.text: There are 12 common shells in each sponson magazine. The mag-

frames.name: p171-text-0431
frames.text: azines on each side of the driver are capable of holding 49 shells.

frames.name: p171-text-0432
frames.text: These are common shells, giving a total of 98 for the two sides in

frames.name: p171-text-0433
frames.text: these magazines. The munition storage in the center of the fighting

frames.name: p171-text-0434
frames.text: compartment is capable of taking 30 shells on each side, giving a

frames.name: p171-text-0437
frames.text: The machine-gun ammunition is distributed between the ammuni-

frames.name: p171-text-0438
frames.text: tion storage space in the center and on the bulkhead between the

frames.name: p171-text-0439
frames.text: engine room and the fighting compartment. The number of racks

frames.name: p171-text-0440
frames.text: contained in the center consists of 21 on the starboard side and 17

frames.name: p171-text-0441
frames.text: on the port side. In the bulkhead between the engine room and the

frames.name: p171-text-0442
frames.text: fighting compartment there are four ammunition racks.

frames.name: p172-text-0466
frames.text: Seven spare machine-gun barrels are carried, one being mounted

frames.name: p172-text-0467
frames.text: in each sponson just forward of the 6-pounder shield. Two are

frames.name: p172-text-0468
frames.text: located in each sponson, forward of the side doors. The machine

frames.name: p172-text-0469
frames.text: guns are dismounted, and carried inside the Mark VIII machine, and

frames.name: p172-text-0470
frames.text: are stored in the following clips for use: One on each sponson, just

frames.name: p172-text-0471
frames.text: forward of the 6-pounder shield; two on each sponson on the rear

frames.name: p172-text-0472
frames.text: plate of same, and one on the port side just forward of the door.

frames.name: p172-text-0474
frames.text: Two British .303 service rifles are stored, one on each side just aft of

frames.name: p172-text-0475
frames.text: the doors and forward of the engine-compartment bulkhead, held by

frames.name: p172-text-0476
frames.text: clips. Stored with these rifles are two smoke-bomb cups to be

frames.name: p172-text-0477
frames.text: fitted to the ends of the rifles, and 80 rounds of .303 special rifle

frames.name: p172-text-0478
frames.text: ammunition for the smoke bombs. There are also 44 rifle smoke

frames.name: p172-text-0479
frames.text: bombs stored in a box under the port door.

frames.name: p172-text-0481
frames.text: SIX-POUNDER GUN SHOWING ALSO AMMUNITION STORAGE

frames.name: p173-text-0484
frames.text: There are two boxes of Hotchkiss spare parts, tools, and appurte-

frames.name: p173-text-0485
frames.text: nances, and each box contains the following:

frames.name: p173-text-0503
frames.text: 1 pin box for small parts M. G.

frames.name: p174-text-0515
frames.text: The trays containing the 6-pounder spare parts are placed on the

frames.name: p174-text-0516
frames.text: floor of the sponson just in the rear of the platform, one tray in each

frames.name: p174-text-0517
frames.text: sponson. These boxes contain the following:

frames.name: p174-text-0522
frames.text: One set of spare parts and tools consisting of the following to be

frames.name: p174-text-0523
frames.text: carried in two trays, one behind each gun:

frames.name: p174-text-0524
frames.text: 1 spanner and screw driver, combined No. 143.

frames.name: p174-text-0540
frames.text: The two 6-pounder guns are carried, one in each sponson. These

frames.name: p174-text-0541
frames.text: guns swing with the sponson, and have an angle of fire from 5° right

frames.name: p174-text-0542
frames.text: of the longitudinal line to 5° aft of the transverse line, or, in other

frames.name: p174-text-0543
frames.text: words, in a 90° arc, moving 5° back from true longitudinal transverse.

frames.name: p174-text-0544
frames.text: The 6-pounder guns can be pulled back within the sponson so that

frames.name: p174-text-0545
frames.text: when the sponsons are swung inboard the guns can be withdrawn

frames.name: p174-text-0546
frames.text: sufficiently to allow the machine to be carried on the railway.

frames.name: p174-text-0548
frames.text: To pull back the 6-pounder guns for railway shipment, first unscrew

frames.name: p174-text-0549
frames.text: the bolts fastening the sponson to the main hull, and push the sponson

frames.name: p174-text-0550
frames.text: inboard from the outside as per directions on page 175. Unscrew the

frames.name: p174-text-0551
frames.text: 12 bolts fastening the gun pivot plate, and the four screws fastening

frames.name: p174-text-0552
frames.text: the training stops to the gun pedestal base plate. Draw the gun,

frames.name: p174-text-0553
frames.text: pivot plate, and shield back as far as desired, and securely fasten to

frames.name: p175-text-0556
frames.text: TO REMOVE AND REPLACE THE 6-POUNDER GUNS

frames.name: p175-text-0557
frames.text: In removing and replacing the 6-pounder guns, remove the “above

frames.name: p175-text-0558
frames.text: platform shell store” to give more room to work. Unscrew the 12

frames.name: p175-text-0559
frames.text: bolts fastening the gun pivot plate and the four screws fastening the

frames.name: p175-text-0560
frames.text: training stops to the gun pedestal base plate. Move the gun and

frames.name: p175-text-0561
frames.text: shield back into the fighting compartment. Remove the shield by

frames.name: p175-text-0562
frames.text: unscrewing the six bolts holding it to the gun mount. The gun and

frames.name: p175-text-0563
frames.text: shield can then be removed separately through the side door. To

frames.name: p175-text-0564
frames.text: replace the gun, put the shield in through one of the side doors, and

frames.name: p175-text-0565
frames.text: then the gun and mounting. Bolt the two together, and place on

frames.name: p175-text-0566
frames.text: top of the gun pedestal base plate and bolt into position.

frames.name: p175-text-0568
frames.text: There are seven Hotchkiss machine guns on the Mark VIII

frames.name: p175-text-0569
frames.text: machine, five of these being in the main turret, one front, one rear,

frames.name: p175-text-0570
frames.text: two on each side, and one located in each of the side doors, in the

frames.name: p175-text-0573
frames.text: To mount the Hotchkiss machine gun in any of the machine

frames.name: p175-text-0574
frames.text: gun posts in the Mark VIII machine, the machine gun is placed in

frames.name: p175-text-0575
frames.text: the mount and pushed forward until the mounting shoulder falls

frames.name: p175-text-0576
frames.text: into the recesses. The gun is then pushed forward and down. This

frames.name: p175-text-0577
frames.text: pushes the locking lug back and the gun falls into place, being held

frames.name: p175-text-0579
frames.text: To remove the machine gun, push forward and up, or turn upside

frames.name: p175-text-0580
frames.text: down so weight will help, which pushes the locking lugs in and releases

frames.name: p175-text-0581
frames.text: the shoulder. The gun can then be removed.

frames.name: p176-text-0584
frames.text: The air for ventilating the fighting compartment is drawn in through

frames.name: p176-text-0585
frames.text: the inlet louver, above the engine, by means of a suction fan, driven

frames.name: p176-text-0586
frames.text: from the crank shaft. The fan is a 7½-inch unit, driven by a link

frames.name: p176-text-0588
frames.text: The intake is drawn in through the front louver, and the air passes

frames.name: p176-text-0589
frames.text: out through the duct to the fan, and thence through a discharge duct

frames.name: p176-text-0590
frames.text: into the fighting compartment, through an opening beneath the

frames.name: p176-text-0591
frames.text: starboard passageway. The fan is located under the side of the engine

frames.name: p176-text-0592

frames.name: p177-text-0652
frames.text: When the machine is ditched the rods are chained to the tracks so

frames.name: p177-text-0653
frames.text: that they move with the tracks. At the rear end of the turret the

frames.name: p177-text-0654
